label: prop:sl2-prolongation-recurrence
title: Symplectic prolongation (det B = 1) gives a one-parameter recurrence
html:
Proposition. Symplectic prolongation (det B = 1) gives a one-parameter recurrence

The recurrence on the prolonged Seiberg--Witten periods has depth 2 (prop:prolonged-periods-fixed-depth together with the S_5-Hodge count H^1 = 2W): the 2\times 2 prolongation operator B on the Hodge multiplicity plane carries the whole kernel, R = x^2 - \mathrm{tr}(B)\,x + \det(B).

The Gauss--Manin monodromy preserves the principal polarisation of the curve — the cup-product symplectic form on H^1, which restricts non-degenerately to the rank-2 W-isotypic Hodge plane (the polarisation is S_5-invariant). Hence B \in \mathrm{Sp}(2) = \mathrm{SL}_2 and

\boxed{\;\det B = 1\;}
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
R = x^2 - \tau\,x + 1,\quad \tau := \mathrm{tr}\, B,

consequently the prolonged periods satisfy the one-parameter "Lucas/Chebyshev" recurrence

a_D^{(n+2)} = \tau\,a_D^{(n+1)} - a_D^{(n)} .

The kernel R is therefore reduced to the single number \tau = \mathrm{tr}\, B, the trace of the prolongation monodromy. The non-hyperbolic torus sector confirms the form: its recurrence is x^2 - 2\cosh(2\eta_0)\,x + 1, i.e. \det = 1 with \tau = 2\cosh(2\eta_0). For the hyperbolic binding sector \tau = 2\cosh\theta for a prolongation rapidity \theta.

Scope: exact for n \le 4, and it fails from n = 5

The symplectic argument stands. B \in \mathrm{Sp}(2) hence \det B = 1, and the formal consequence, B^{2} = \tau B - 1 propagating to B^{n+2} = \tau B^{n+1} - B^{n}, is proved for every n in the Lean sibling. What that establishes is an implication: if the prolonged periods are generated by a depth-2 symplectic operator, then they obey the recurrence. The premise is what is limited.

The prolonged periods have a closed form of their own,

a_D^{(n)} = \frac{S(n)}{n},
\qquad S(n) = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} \dim_q \lambda ,

(prop:sw-period-residue-sum), with no free parameter and no anchor input. That object grows super-exponentially, while any depth-2 recurrence with \det = 1 grows geometrically, at a ratio tending to the larger root of R. The two cannot agree for large n. Evaluated at the proton pin with \tau \approx 2.6423863, iterating from the true a_D^{(2)}, a_D^{(3)}:

n recurrence closed form S(n)/n deviation
4 2.532779656 2.532779656 0.0\%
5 5.355616667 5.376137730 -0.38\%
6 11.61882850 13.55982713 -14.31\%
7 25.34581670 37.36780738 -32.17\%
8 55.35461055 115.8262242 -52.21\%

The depth-2 form is therefore an n \le 4 effective germ, and the prolongation law carrying the true growth is the residue-sum object itself. This is the reading already recorded downstream in prop:sl2-period-conserved-quantity, which uses this block: a factorial sequence has unbounded ratio a_D^{(n+1)}/a_D^{(n)}, so it satisfies no depth-2 recurrence, and the exact prolongation kernel is of q-Bessel class.

Two consequences follow for how \tau should be read.

\tau is determined, but it is not informative. Because each a_D^{(n)} is a closed form, \tau = (a_D^{(2)} + a_D^{(4)})/a_D^{(3)} evaluates to a number with no input beyond q. But that expression is the n = 2 instance of the recurrence rearranged, so the n = 4 row above is true by construction and is not a test of the form: substituting any value whatever for a_D^{(3)} leaves the n = 4 residual identically zero.

\theta is not an open number of the depth correspondence. The sequence a_D^{(n)} is determined for every n without \tau, so \tau is a summary of three of its terms rather than a missing input.
